DearSion Buckler,

Thank you for your enquiry in which you asked for the information concerning the existence, provenance, transfer, retention, destruction or disposal of records relating to Ty Mawr / Great House Farm.

Your request has been handled under the Freedom of Information (FOI) Act 2000. The FOI Act gives you the right to know whether we hold the information you want and to have it communicated to you, subject to any exemptions which may apply.

I can confirm that The National Archives holds some information relevant to your request. We are pleased to be able to provide some of this information to you.

Our response

The initial response from our records enquiries team looked for the four terms (“Great House Farm”, “Ty Mawr”, “Llandough” or “Cedfin”) within the PRO and RW series and did not find any relevant information. We have now tried those terms and the further twelve terms that you have specified in a wider catalogue search. We have provided the results of our search below.

The crux of your query is local land ownership dispute in Glamorgan and the demolition of some buildings by a private company; generally speaking, these are not matters dealt with by central government and we would not expect to see anything within our collections. As such, there would have been no records to transfer. The exception is the court case relating to BP properties, which generated some papers. Links to the catalogue pages for these records can be seen below.

There are likely to be records of the farm in the 1940s as part of the National Farm Survey series but these cannot all currently be searched online by farm.

We are unable to conduct this research on the archival collections on your behalf without charging fees to conduct research on your behalf (Paid Search). A public authority is allowed to charge fees under section 9 of the Freedom of Information Act and within this section of the Act it states: "provision is made by or under any enactment as to the fee may be charged by the public authority for the disclosure of the information" (S9(5) FOIA).

The Public Records Act (1958) enables a statutory instrument to be made setting out the fees which may be made in connection with the supply of information from The National Archives. The prices we charge are set out by our Fees Regulations<https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/1243/made>.

If you are interested in paying for research to be conducted on your behalf, then details of our Paid Search service and other options for paying for research are available here: Paying for research - The National Archives<https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/paying-for-research/>

If you would prefer to conduct this research yourself then you may find the following research guide to be of assistance: National Farm Survey of England and Wales 1941-1943 - The National Archives<https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/research-guides/national-farm-survey-england-wales-1941-1943/>

There are Agricultural Executive Committee minutes and papers for Glamorgan; but again, these cannot be searched online by name of farm and we are unable to conduct this research without charging a fee: Browse records of other archives | The National Archives<https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/browse/r/h/C42711>

We can provide the following advice regarding the search terms you have specified:


  1.  Western Ground Rents Ltd

      Relevant information not found.


  2.  BP Pension Trust Ltd

      Relevant information not found.


  3.  BP Properties Ltd

      Judicial Papers A-C 1-63 | The National Archives<https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/74c935f9-563a-4c1b-8643-ed3eed68ad98> (House of Lords as court of appeal)


  4.  Mountjoy Ltd

      Relevant information not found.


  5.  Proceedings in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2

      Judicial Papers A-C 1-63 | The National Archives<https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/74c935f9-563a-4c1b-8643-ed3eed68ad98> (House of Lords as court of appeal)


  6.  1982–1983 registration and associated government or administrative records

      Relevant information not found.


  7.  1980–1988 public campaign and governmental correspondence

      Relevant information not found.


  8.  1988 eviction and demolition

      Relevant information not found.


  9.  Cadw or central-government communications concerning the property

      Relevant information not found.


  10. European Commission of Human Rights Application 14464/88

      Relevant information not found.


  11. Records concerning transfer, destruction or disposal of potentially relevant material

      Within the results of our search, it revealed a record within the parliamentary collection.

      This is Judicial Papers A-C 1-63<https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/74c935f9-563a-4c1b-8643-ed3eed68ad98> . The parliamentary records and the provision of a service for them by The National Archives, was done in phases, with their collections loaded into Discovery in stages. The series that this record formed part of were released on our catalogue on Discovery on 20th May 2026.

      This is an open record and available to the public here at The National Archives, Kew. To note, this record requires preparation for production and will take four working days to prepare

      TNA holds transfer paperwork for YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536 - Judicial Papers A-C 1-63<https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/74c935f9-563a-4c1b-8643-ed3eed68ad98>. The below table is a schedule of the documents that we have attached to this response.

        Relevant information to request provided. Some of the information is additionally redacted as ‘out of scope’ and not relevant to the request.

Item 03 Collect 27 Series 11 Spreadsheet: Manifest
This spreadsheet is the manifest TNA received from the Parliamentary Archives   Relevant information to request provided. Some of the information is additionally redacted as ‘out of scope’ and not relevant to the request.



  12. HMC9/311 or related archival references

      This is Manorial Documents register returns the county of Glamorgan organised by Manor alphabetically. The Manorial Documents Register<https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/manor-search> can now be searched online, by manor or parish and the results display in Discovery.  This search summary █████ it lists records 1189-1925 held at National Library of Wales, Glamorgan Archives and West Glamorgan Archive Service: Search results: llandough | The National Archives<https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/results/c?_q=llandough&_sf=text_man&_naet=M&_st=mdrc>. This date range is too early, individual farm names are not listed in the titles, and the records are not held at TNA.

This is the limit of what our catalogue metadata and corporate records allow us to confirm.

This concludes our response to your request.

FOI Assessor

Government and Archives Leadership

Your request

Original email dated 13/08/2026:

My request was deliberately framed more broadly than a simple catalogue search for the words “Great House Farm”, “Ty Mawr”, “Llandough” or “Cedfin”. I specifically asked The National Archives to identify recorded information concerning the existence, transfer, retention, destruction, disposal or absence of records, including records that might not be catalogued under the property's later or local names.

Your response confirms only that you searched the PRO and RW series using:

“Great House Farm” OR “Ty Mawr” OR Llandough OR Cedfin

combined with “Glamorgan”, and that this produced no catalogue results.

You also correctly state that Discovery searches catalogue titles and descriptions rather than the contents of records. That qualification is important, because it means the search described cannot establish that relevant records did not exist, were never transferred, or were destroyed.

In particular, your response does not appear to address the other categories expressly identified in my request, including searches or recorded information relating to:


   *   Western Ground Rents Ltd;
   *   BP Pension Trust Ltd;
   *   BP Properties Ltd;
   *   Mountjoy Ltd;
   *   the proceedings in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2;
   *   the 1982–1983 registration and associated government or administrative records;
   *   the 1980–1988 public campaign and governmental correspondence;
   *   the 1988 eviction and demolition;
   *   Cadw or central-government communications concerning the property;
   *   European Commission of Human Rights Application 14464/88;
   *   records concerning transfer, destruction or disposal of potentially relevant material; and
   *   HMC9/311 or related archival references.

These alternative lines of enquiry are intentional. The purpose is to establish whether relevant information can be identified through the government bodies, corporate entities, court proceedings, administrative processes and archival transfers associated with the property, rather than relying solely upon the modern name by which the property is known.

I am conducting corresponding enquiries with other repositories and public bodies. This is specifically intended to triangulate the documentary history where records may have been catalogued under a different creator, department, legal proceeding, estate, corporate body or administrative function.

I therefore ask that you do not treat the absence of a Discovery keyword hit as an answer to the substantive questions raised.

Please clarify:


  1.  Whether the searches undertaken were limited to the PRO and RW catalogue series and the four property/location search terms identified in your email.


  2.  Whether The National Archives searched for the named corporate bodies, court proceedings and application references identified in my request, rather than only searching the property names.


  3.  Whether The National Archives holds any recorded transfer, accession, disposal, destruction or retention information indicating that records concerning the relevant property, estate, companies, litigation or government involvement were transferred elsewhere, destroyed, or otherwise disposed of.


  4.  If such information is not held, whether this is because no such records are held, because no relevant records were ever transferred to TNA, or because TNA's catalogue/search systems contain no discoverable description of them.


  5.  Whether HMC9/311 or related series have been checked, or whether that reference falls outside the search undertaken.


  6.  Whether there are central-government, court, departmental or administrative records relating to the litigation and entities identified above which may contain references to the property without using “Great House Farm”, “Ty Mawr”, “Llandough” or “Cedfin” in the catalogue description.

For the avoidance of doubt, I am not asking The National Archives to infer the contents of uncatalogued records or to undertake an unlimited research project. I am asking for confirmation of the recorded information held by TNA concerning the existence, provenance, transfer, retention, destruction or disposal of potentially relevant records, and for the searches undertaken to locate that information.

That distinction is particularly important because a catalogue search returning no result is not equivalent to a finding that no relevant historical, governmental or archival records existed.

I would therefore be grateful if this could be reconsidered as a response to the scope of the original FOI enquiry rather than treated solely as a request for assistance with a Discovery keyword search.

I am continuing parallel enquiries with the National Library of Wales, Glamorgan Archives, Cadw, RCAHMW, HM Land Registry and other relevant bodies. The purpose of these enquiries is to establish the documentary chain independently and to identify where records were created, transferred, retained or potentially destroyed.

Follow-up email dated 20/08/2026

In addition, please expand the scope of the search to include any records held relating to the Glamorgan War Agricultural Executive Committee (“War Ag” / CWAEC) and Great House Farm / the relevant land at Llandough, covering approximately 1936–1950 (with particular focus on 1939–1945). This should include, where held:


   *   Any orders, notices or decisions taking possession of, directing cultivation of, or otherwise requisitioning land forming part of Great House Farm (or the specific parcel now associated with Llandough Motor Sales / Llandough Trading Estate).
   *   Any compensation █████, assessments, payments or settlements under the Compensation (Defence) Act 1939 or related wartime legislation, including the identity of the recipient(s).
   *   Relevant minutes, correspondence or case files of the Glamorgan CWAEC concerning the farm or land in question.
   *   Any related material in the MAF series that links the National Farm Survey entries with wartime agricultural possession or compensation.

I hold original documents recording compensation payments in connection with this land and am seeking to identify the wartime status of the holding and the party recognised as entitled to compensation.

Clarification email dated 02/09/2026

In summary, I am seeking recorded information held by The National Archives concerning:


   *   Existence, transfer, retention, destruction or disposal of records relating to Great House Farm / Ty Mawr (and earlier descriptions) and associated entities, litigation and administrative processes (as previously detailed).


   *   National Farm Survey / MAFF records for the holding.


   *   Any Glamorgan CWAEC / War Ag records, possession/requisition orders, cultivation directions, and compensation █████/payments under the Compensation (Defence) Act 1939 or related wartime legislation in respect of the land (or the parcel now associated with Llandough Motor Sales / Llandough Trading Estate), including identity of any compensation recipients.

I am not asking for an open-ended research exercise. I am asking for confirmation of what recorded information (including transfer, accession, disposal or destruction records) is held, the series searched, and the results of those searches.

FIREWORKS: WESTPOINT INDUSTRIAL ESTATE


**
------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Requester

Thursday night's incident, in which fireworks were set off again at WestPoint Industrial Estate, was completely unacceptable.

People from outside Llandough coming into our community and behaving in such a selfish and inconsiderate manner is becoming an increasing problem.

It shows no regard for the way we do things in Llandough.

We rightly think of others, recognising the impacts our actions can have on some of the most vulnerable members of our community.
Those responsible showed no such regard.

The images above, captured by Peter Griffiths of Vale Sports Arena, demonstrate the extent of the problem.

They show both the number of fireworks set off and the number of people involved.

It also shows authorities must treat stopping this behaviour as a priority.

The noise caused is distressing for many people, including the elderly and those with small children.

It's also distressing for animals, which is a particular problem with Cardiff Dogs Home located within the vicinity.

https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1F4JUgcVux/

I've contacted both South Wales Police and the Vale of Glamorgan Council to request the following things:
* Effective surveillance equipment be installed urgently to identify those responsible;
* Regular nighttime police patrols in the area to stop and apprehend those causing these disturbances;
* Access to the area to be limited to prevent people using it to set off fireworks.

It is a criminal offence to set off fireworks past 11pm at night.

There are also many other laws and regulations that may have been broken.

While Thursday's incident commenced at around 10.30pm, there have been several previous instances in which the law has clearly been breached.

It is punishable by an unlimited fine and up to six months imprisonment.

It is time for the law to be enforced.

Those responsible for causing distress to the vulnerable in Llandough cannot be allowed to think the law does not apply to them.

If you any information about this incident, Requester, please come forward. It will be treated in the utmost confidence.


**
------------------------------------------------------------

NEXT WEEK:
Redlands Road diversion

Redlands Road will be closed between 9th and 11th October to vehicles travelling towards Dinas Powys towards Llandough.

This is because the right hand turn will be closed to allow gas works to be carried out safely.

Details of the diversion can be found above.

As you'll see, drivers are being told to travel past the Merrie Harrier and the Barons Court to the Cardiff Bay roundabout, where they will be able to turn around and travel back towards Penarth, before using the left hand turn to access Redlands Road.

The route for vehicles travelling in the opposite direction is unaffected.

While this is unlikely to be particularly problematic for Llandough residents, I'm concerned some drivers may attempt to use the Dochdwy estate or the Merrie Harrier car park to turn around, potentially causing a bottleneck.

I've therefore put together a short video, explaining the diversion route in place, which avoids our village.

It would be helpful if you would share it on social media, Requester.

To do so, you can click below now.
https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1CJhqM9XTD/

Road markings:
Pen-y-turnpike Road

The road markings at the junction between Pen-y-turnpike Road and Leckwith Road have now been repainted.

We secured these works together, by pressuring the Council to get them done.

It may seem like a small thing, but making it clear to drivers they need to give way will help stop accidents.

Thank you to everyone across Llandough, Leckwith and Michaelston-le-Pit who helped.
https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1EaRtbbAVJ/

Preventing overdevelopment

When I'm out and about in our community, many residents express concerns about overdevelopment and the way it threatens our village's distinct identity and character.

The proposals to build 250 houses on Eastbrook Road are a good example.

While outside our village, the site is located just down from the Merrie Harrier, on green fields that form a natural boundary between Llandough and Dinas Powys.

This boundary is crucial in ensuring both villages remain separate, unique entities.

You can watch my comments at the last Full Council meeting below.

https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1Fff7ZbyuK/

Dochdwy Road pavement defects

Huge thanks to the resident who got in touch about pavement defects on Dochdwy Road.

As you'll see, these have now all been marked up for repair.

By getting in touch, the resident helped ensure the issue was taken forward quickly.

When you contact me about things you spot, you're not causing a bother.

To the contrary, you're playing a crucial role in our team, as we work to improve things in our village.

That's what Our Plan for Llandough is all about!

https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1Hy7k64Xw5/

Community drop-in event:
20th October

Our next community drop-in event takes place at the Merrie Harrier on 20th October.

Like the last one, it'll start at 7.00pm.

The pub is a key asset to our community.

Tracey and the team do a lot for us - help return the favour by lending them your support.

You can see some of their midweek offers below!

https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1EM9z5wbMs/

Our Plan for Llandough!


As your councillor, I'm working with you all to secure a better future for Llandough. Together, we have a plan to deliver for the village.

Our plan is making Llandough better by:

1. Sorting out the parking problems
2. Stamping out dog fouling
3. Repairing our roads
4. Stopping littering and flytipping
5. Delivering better sports facilities
6. Keeping the whole community involved

Amgueddfa Cymru has previously responded to requests concerning Great House Farm / Ty Mawr / Llandough Farm, Llandough, including FOI 2026-024 and FOI 2026-032. Collections staff reviewed records identified through references to Great House Farm, Ty Mawr and Llandough Farm, Llandough (Vale of Glamorgan), together with records returned through associated place-name searches. Dear Requester,

With regards to your email of 30th September, I note that many of the queries which you have set have already been addressed in our previous correspondence. In particular, please note that our searches have been extensive, including searches of any possibly relevant registered files, the only administrative and operational records and materials held in the long term, and the NMRW archive, including both term-based and spatial searches in the archive catalogue, and a manual search for any additional, uncatalogued material. This will be more fully addressed in point 1 as I take your questions in order, below.

1) Our searches have been extensive. This has included searches of any possibly relevant registered files, the only administrative records and materials held in the long term. As I have noted, we do not appear to hold any records or correspondence in these records relating to your enquiries, or to Great House Farm more generally, including the circumstances of its demolition. Our searches have also included full searches of the NMRW archive, including both term-based and spatial searches in the archive catalogue, and a manual search for any additional, uncatalogued material. The term-based searches have included all relevant site names and related terms, as you have enumerated them. These searches have therefore included searches for all of the types of records which you have enumerated, with the exception of our historic aerial photography collections, which searches would incur a charge (see point 6, below).

2) As has been noted in my previous correspondence, no record of this correspondence or allusion to the same is extant in our records, with the exception of the brief note in Archive 6048945. For the scope of our comprehensive searches undertaken to determine this, see point 1, above.

3) Regarding Archive Number 6048945, as I noted in my email of 29 September, if you would like to order a scan of this record, please complete the attached order form. The record comprises one page, front and back, and would therefore require two scans. Please note that we waive fees for small orders of fewer than 5 research-quality scans for personal, non-commercial research. The record is part of our NMR Site Files Collection, for details of which, please see the collection-level entry in our archive catalogue, here: https://coflein.gov.uk/en/archives/6202405. As I further noted in my email of 29 September, there is no surviving record giving the date or purpose of that visit beyond the description currently catalogued, nor any associated site note, field sheet, photograph, sketch or correspondence.

4) Searches of our internal records relating to these accessions numbers have revealed no further information beyond that which is available in the publicly accessible archive catalogue and noted in my email of 29th September.

5) These records have been thoroughly, physically reviewed and it has been determined that they relate to the sites stated in the Archive Catalogue. They do not relate or allude to Great House Farm, Llandough in any way.

6) With regard to aerial photography, as noted in my email of 29 September, a search of our aerial photography collections, including to determine whether there is aerial photography coverage of the site, would incur a charge (see attached price list). As was further noted in my email of 29 September, if any aerial photographs covering the area of the site do exist, these would likely be vertical aerial photography, taken from a high altitude during routine recording of the landscape and would be unlikely to show the site in any detail. There is no further photographic record of the site in our collection.

7) As noted in previous correspondence, the 1974 ‘investigator's notes for Great House Farm, Llandough, including sketch plan showing periods of construction’ by H. J. Thomas is Archive Number 6048943 (https://coflein.gov.uk/en/archives/6048943). The ‘ink drawing showing plan of Great House Farm, Llandough, showing periods of construction. Scale 1:100. Additions made 12/12/1988’ is Archive Number 6048941 (https://coflein.gov.uk/en/archives/6048941). A scan of the item Archive Number 6048943 can be ordered using the attached order form, while, as noted in my emails of 28 May and 29 September, a copy of Archive Number 6048941 is included in the report available here: https://www.walesher1974.org/her/app/php/herumd.php?group=GGAT&level=3&docid=301361628. As I have noted throughout our correspondence, we do not hold anything beyond the material already visible on Coflein.

8) There is no record of this.

9) We hold no such providence information.

10) As noted in my email of 29 September and in point 3, above, we do not hold any information relating to the circumstances of the December 1988 visit outside of Archive Number 6048945.

11) See point 1, above. Physical searches were undertaken of all relevant Registered Files and key collections, such as the Site Files, which may have contained uncatalogued material. In both cases nothing of any relevance was identified beyond the records enumerated in the online archive catalogue here: https://coflein.gov.uk/en/sites/20182/archives. Comprehensive searches were carried out on both Coflein and Historic Wales, as well as in our internal archive catalogue and details of these searches are noted in point 1, above. All identified archive material has been carefully examined and read by our enquiries staff. All relevant records and archive staff have been consulted. No potentially relevant material has been excluded for any reason.

12) In accordance with the suggestion contained in your email of 20 September, my email of 29 September fully addressed, and was in reply to, all enquiries of 8, 15, 17, and 20 September, and I therefore consider all of these enquiries to have now received a full response. We have established that we hold no internal, administrative, or operational records related to your enquiries, nor any which relate to Great House Farm, and that the only records of any relevance which we hold are publicly accessible records in the National Monuments Record of Wales archives. FIREWORKS: WESTPOINT INDUSTRIAL ESTATE


**
------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Requester

Thursday night's incident, in which fireworks were set off again at WestPoint Industrial Estate, was completely unacceptable.

People from outside Llandough coming into our community and behaving in such a selfish and inconsiderate manner is becoming an increasing problem.

It shows no regard for the way we do things in Llandough.

We rightly think of others, recognising the impacts our actions can have on some of the most vulnerable members of our community.
Those responsible showed no such regard.

The images above, captured by Peter Griffiths of Vale Sports Arena, demonstrate the extent of the problem.

They show both the number of fireworks set off and the number of people involved.

It also shows authorities must treat stopping this behaviour as a priority.

The noise caused is distressing for many people, including the elderly and those with small children.

It's also distressing for animals, which is a particular problem with Cardiff Dogs Home located within the vicinity.

https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1F4JUgcVux/

I've contacted both South Wales Police and the Vale of Glamorgan Council to request the following things:
* Effective surveillance equipment be installed urgently to identify those responsible;
* Regular nighttime police patrols in the area to stop and apprehend those causing these disturbances;
* Access to the area to be limited to prevent people using it to set off fireworks.

It is a criminal offence to set off fireworks past 11pm at night.

There are also many other laws and regulations that may have been broken.

While Thursday's incident commenced at around 10.30pm, there have been several previous instances in which the law has clearly been breached.

It is punishable by an unlimited fine and up to six months imprisonment.

It is time for the law to be enforced.

Those responsible for causing distress to the vulnerable in Llandough cannot be allowed to think the law does not apply to them.

If you any information about this incident, Requester, please come forward. It will be treated in the utmost confidence.

This boundary is crucial in ensuring both villages remain separate, unique entities.

You can watch my comments at the last Full Council meeting below.

https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1Fff7ZbyuK/

As you'll see, these have now all been marked up for repair.

By getting in touch, the resident helped ensure the issue was taken forward quickly.

When you contact me about things you spot, you're not causing a bother.

20th October

Our next community drop-in event takes place at the Merrie Harrier on 20th October.

To each recipient separately, in your own capacity as a current or potential holder, custodian or controller of relevant records:

This notice is addressed to each recipient individually. It is not a joint request, and it does not ask any recipient to speak for, investigate on behalf of, or answer in place of any other person or organisation. Each recipient is asked to respond only in respect of records within that recipient's own possession, custody or control, including records inherited from a predecessor organisation or retained on its behalf.

1. Nature and purpose of this notice

This is a formal preservation notice concerning documentary material relating to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy's, and the subsequent development of the site, including the area now associated with Church View Close.

It is not a claim form, is not service of proceedings, and is not intended to constitute or replace any FOI request, internal review, complaint, subject-access request or other statutory process already made to any recipient.

The purpose of this notice is to require the preservation of potentially relevant material while the documentary history, title chain, registration history, planning history, possession proceedings, demolition and subsequent development are being reconstructed.

A separate first-stage preservation notice has been issued or is being issued to Cadw / Welsh Government FOI, HM Land Registry Wales Office and DPO, Heneb / GGAT HER, RCAHMW, Vale of Glamorgan FOI Unit and DPO, Glamorgan Archives, South Wales Police FOI, The National Archives, the Wales Office FOI team, and the National Library of Wales. Persimmon Homes (Wales) Ltd has received a separate preservation letter.

You are receiving this notice separately because the published documentary record places you, or a predecessor whose records may remain in your custody or control, within the documentary, legal, professional, administrative or development chain concerning this land.

2. Land and documentary scope

Please preserve, and do not destroy, alter, overwrite, discard, transfer out of custody without a recorded handover, or otherwise dispose of, any record within your possession, custody or control relating to the land or matters identified below.

The scope includes, without limitation, originals, copies, working papers, drafts, annotations, plans, photographs, negatives, films, tapes, maps, registers, indexes, correspondence, emails and attachments, electronic files, archived mailboxes, databases, metadata, internal notes, meeting records, instructions, client or matter files, survey material and other associated records.

The material requested includes:

1. Historical ownership, occupation and conveyancing

The 1877 split; the 1916 and 1939 tenancies; the 1938 Bute to Western Ground Rents conveyance; the 1969 Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust conveyance; and any plans, schedules, abstracts, searches, correspondence or other documents relied upon in relation to those transactions.

2. Possession proceedings and subsequent litigation

The █████ and █████ possession orders; the 1974 proceedings; BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2; House of Lords leave papers, including YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536; and Buckler v United Kingdom (1989), including associated correspondence, instructions, evidence, plans and working papers.

3. Land registration

The first registration of WA231076, including the application dated 30 November 1982; the first registration of WA240304, including the application dated 23 February 1983; subsequent amalgamation, transfer or closure; and every plan, conveyance, abstract, search, application, correspondence trail or professional file relied upon in connection with those registrations or changes.

4. 1988 possession and demolition

The taking of possession on or about 29 November 1988 and the demolition commenced on or about 6 December 1988, including any planning, listed-building, heritage, police, enforcement, media, contractor, survey, photographic or inter-agency liaison material.

5. Planning and subsequent development, 1989–1996

Planning application 89/01396/OUT; reserved matters application 92/00671/RES; conditions 16–18; GGAT / Cotswold Archaeology material; records concerning any section 52, section 106, planning obligation, local land charge or equivalent instrument; and the transfer from BP to Ideal Homes dated 3 December 1993, together with all associated plans, correspondence, approvals, agreements, searches and completion material.

6. Family records

Records concerning Mary Doreen Williams (died 1983) and William Buckler, insofar as those records relate to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, the land described above, its occupation, ownership, possession, disposal, registration, development or demolition.

3. Predecessor and inherited files

Where you hold, or may hold, a file originating with a predecessor, successor, merged practice, affiliated practice, client or other entity, that material is also within scope.

4. Preservation steps

Please take reasonable steps to prevent the routine destruction, deletion, alteration or overwriting of potentially relevant material, including material held in archived mailboxes, legacy systems, off-site storage, document-management systems, backup repositories and other electronic or physical stores.

Where relevant material has been transferred to another repository, archive, successor organisation or third party, please preserve the information necessary to identify the transfer and its current location, including any accession, file, box, reference or custody details.

Nothing in this notice requires the creation of records that do not exist. The request concerns the preservation of records already held or controlled by you.

5. Purpose and legal position

This notice is not a finding against any recipient, and I am not asking any recipient to determine title or adjudicate the underlying dispute.

The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment is relied upon here only for matters actually determined by that judgment, including the issues concerning possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. This preservation notice does not treat that judgment as having determined the complete documentary root of title to the farmhouse parcel.

The underlying documentary history, including the relationship between the farmhouse parcel and the agricultural land subsequently dealt with through Western Ground Rents and BP, remains a matter requiring reconstruction from the primary records.

Accordingly, preservation is requested precisely so that the documentary record can be established from the records themselves rather than through assumptions based on later registration, later occupation, later planning treatment or secondary descriptions.

records.transcript:
Dear Requester,

Thank you for your email of  21 September 2026 making a request for 
information.

We are treating your correspondence as a request for information under 
the Freedom of Information Act 2000 (the act).

Under the provisions of the act and as defined by "The Freedom of 
Information and Data Protection (Appropriate Limit and Fees) Regulations 
2004" (the regulations) , an authority is not obliged to comply with a 
request for information if the authority estimates that the cost of 
complying with the request would exceed the "appropriate limit".  This 
appropriate limit is set by the regulations at £450 for our type of 
authority.

In the regulations our staff time is valued at £25 per hour.  This has 
the effect of imposing a time limit of 18 hours of staff time for 
activities specified in the regulations.

  The regulations make the following activities by an authority countable 
towards the cost limit.

  	* determining whether it holds the information,

  	* locating the information, or a document which may contain the 
information,

  	* retrieving the information, or a document which may contain the 
information, and

  	* extracting the information from a document containing it.

  We have estimated the time and therefore costs as provided by the 
regulations, and in doing so have taken into account the above 
activities.

  We estimate that this work will take in excess of 18 hours of effort by 
our staff. As we have a significant amount of documents on file from the 
period 2002-2016 where minutes are in documents rather than published on 
the website or in archives.

  We estimate this will exceed the limit provided for by the regulations 
and therefore your request is refused on the grounds provided for under 
section 12 of the act.

Our estimate of time is based on the requirement to search all minutes 
of the council and its committees for a period of 14 years. It is 
estimated that it will take about 20 minutes to read each set of minutes 
of which there are estimated to 224 sets of minutes. It is considered 
that this is likely to take about 10 minutes to assess each set of 
minutes a total of over 2240 minutes which equates to 37 hours.

  We may may be able to provide some information if you are able to 
reduce or refine your request to bring the cost of compliance under the 
regulations limit.  We suggest that you could limit the time frame of 
minutes that we would need to look through. For example 2002-2006.

  Please contact us if you would like to refine your request.

  If you are not satisfied with this response or you wish to complain 
about any aspect of the handling of your request, then you should 
contact us in the first instance and we will undertake an internal 
review.

  If after the internal review you wish to complain further then you can 
complain to the Information Commissioners Office http://www.ico.gov.uk 
[1] and request a decision notice.

The other matters you include in your email will be considered at the 
October meeting of the council and I will let you have the views of the 
council after the meeting.

  Kind regards,
---
Paul R. Egan BA, Chartered MCIPD, CiLCA, F. Inst. LM, FIPSM

Clerk to Llandough Community Council,

[address removed]

Vale of Glamorgan █████

Telephone █████

Website www.llandough-cc.co.uk [2]

When you contact us

The information you provide (personal information such as name, address,
email address, phone number, organisation) will be processed and stored
to enable us to contact you and respond to your correspondence, provide
information and/or access our facilities and services.

Your personal information will be not shared or provided to any other 
third party. Your information may however be published in the public

For further information please see our full privacy notice on our

The Council's mission statement is 'Serving our community, preserving

· Be accountable in all our council activities

· Be responsive to the needs of the community

· Encourage community participation

On 2026-09-21 03:59, Requester wrote:

> Dr Misra,
> 
> Thank you for replying, and for doing so promptly and at a weekend. 
> Good drills Sir. What an honour. I know you and the Council serve as 
> volunteers, and I am grateful for the time.
> 
> Let me set out plainly what I am asking of the Council, which is 
> narrow. If you'll allow me?
> 
> I am not asking your Council to revisit Mr Egan's answer of 14 June 
> 2026. He explained that the minute books from 1982 onwards were 
> deposited with Glamorgan Archives in 2002, and I am pursuing those 
> there.
> 
> What I am asking about is what that answer did not cover. Llandough 
> Community Council is a public authority under Schedule 1, Part II, 
> paragraph 7(b) of the Freedom of Information Act 2000. The Act applies 
> to the recorded information set out below generally; the Environmental 
> Information Regulations 2004 apply in addition to any part of it that 
> is environmental information.
> 
> PART ONE -- REQUEST FOR RECORDED INFORMATION
> 
> 1. Whether the Council holds any recorded information created after the 
> 2002 deposit -- minutes, correspondence, reports, emails, photographs 
> or files of any kind -- concerning Great House Farm (Ty Mawr) / Church 
> View Close, the village green in front of St Dochdwy's including 
> registered green VG 41, or the roadside verge by the churchyard wall.
> 
> 2. Whether the Council holds any photographs, postcards or images of 
> the farm, the barn, the green or the church surroundings, of any date.
> 
> 3. Whether the Council holds any recorded information showing what, if 
> anything, transferred to it from Penarth Town Council at the 1982 
> reorganisation, and any recorded information identifying where the 
> pre-1982 Llandough community records were deposited.
> 
> If the answer to any of these is that no such information is held, I 
> would be content with a short statement to that effect -- but I do need 
> it stated. Section 1(1)(a) of the Act requires the Council to confirm 
> or deny whether the information is held.
> 
> Section 10 (and regulation 5 of the EIR) allows twenty working days 
> from receipt, which on my request of 20 September 2026 I calculate as 
> 16 October 2026.
> 
> If the Council is refusing, section 17 (and regulation 14) requires a 
> written refusal notice identifying the exemption or exception relied 
> on; section 17(7) requires the Council to give particulars of any 
> complaints procedure it operates, or to state that it has none, and to 
> notify me of my right to apply to the Information Commissioner; and 
> regulation 11 gives a right to an internal review of any refusal under 
> the EIR.
> 
> "We have nothing more to add" does not meet those requirements. If the 
> period passes without a compliant response I will have no option but to 
> complain to the Information Commissioner.
> 
> PART TWO -- MATTERS FOR THE COUNCIL'S DISCRETION
> 
> These are not part of the request above and carry no deadline. They are 
> simply things I would be grateful for.
> 
> A. I am not asking for the name or contact details of any individual. I 
> am asking whether the Council would be willing to pass my details to 
> any former member, former clerk or long-standing resident who might 
> remember the village between the 1950s and the 1990s, leaving it 
> entirely to them whether to contact me. I appreciate the Council may 
> have data protection or administrative reasons for declining, and I 
> would not press it.
> 
> B. Whether the Council would be willing to table this correspondence at 
> a meeting and minute it. I am content for it to be tabled in full.
> 
> C. Whether the Council would consider, in due course, whether an 
> interpretation board or a plaque near the green would be appropriate. 
> The excavation on the land beneath Church View Close recorded 1,026 
> burials, described in the published report as by far the largest early 
> medieval burial population so far recovered from Wales, above a Roman 
> villa and an Iron Age roundhouse. That history belongs to Llandough as 
> much as to my family, and there is nothing on the ground that records 
> it. I would be glad to give the Council or the community a short talk 
> on the documentary record, without charge, if that would be useful.
> 
> I should be grateful for a response to items 1 to 3 by 16 October 2026.
> 
> Regards,
> 
> Requester

Dear Requester,

Many thanks for your e-mail below and your request for Scrutiny to consider the topic suggested as part of it's Task and Finish work.

Unfortunately, on this occasion we will be unable to consider the request for several reasons:

1. The purpose of Task and Finish is to review existing policy Council considerations and identify areas for future policy direction at a strategic level impacting on a county wide basis. These topics are purposefully strategic in manner, and are based upon areas that Committees determine to have the most positive impact.

2. In addition to the above, the purpose of Scrutiny is not to review evidence related to individual historical decisions and make subsequent recommendations, particularly related to planning, which should be navigated through other channels.

3. We are aware through other correspondence to which you have copied us into that there are ongoing concerns being raised through a variety of channels including Welsh Government, CADW, MSs and MPs, and as such it would not be appropriate for a Scrutiny Task and Finish to add an additional layer of stakeholders and complexity in exploring the issues; notwithstanding points 1 and 2 raised.

Kind Regards,
James

Dear Democratic and Scrutiny Services,

Scrutiny Topic Suggestion / request for a focused Task and Finish Review

I am a resident with a long-standing family connection to Great House Farm (Tÿ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth. A public documentary archive of the site is maintained at:

https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/

I request that the Council consider a focused Scrutiny Topic Suggestion leading to a Task and Finish Review (or other appropriate scrutiny mechanism) concerning the Council-held planning, heritage, environmental and public-authority record relating to Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr / Church View Close.

Proposed scope (within the Council’s remit):

• the Council-held planning, heritage, environmental and public-authority record relating to Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr / Church View Close; • the chronology of Council decisions, records and responses from the mid-twentieth century onwards; • identification of missing, contradictory or unresolved Council-held records and, where appropriate, referral to the body with the relevant jurisdiction; • consideration of the site’s heritage and historical record, including its proposed interpretation in the Tÿ Mawr replica museum project in Puerto Madryn, Chubut; and • recommendations within the Council’s powers, without asking the Council to determine private title, criminal liability or matters reserved to courts or other public bodies.

This is an evidence-review and accountability route. It is not a request for the Council to decide private title or liability.

I am happy to complete the online Scrutiny Topic Suggestion Form if preferred, or to supply any further information the Democratic Services team requires.

Please acknowledge receipt and indicate the process and timescale for consideration.

Kind regards,

Requester
